children: Malaysian glove sector's near-term outlook could be turning less cautious as cost pass-through improves, driven by rising selling prices and easing competition from China, says Maybank IB analyst Wong Wei Sum in a note. Glove prices have risen to between $19 and $20 per 1,000 pieces in September and could reach the $22-$23 range in October, helping offset higher raw-material costs, she says. Chinese competitor Intco Medical Technology has also raised prices, and higher coal costs there could further ease pressure from Chinese producers, she reckons. However, the extent of margin protection will depend on whether Malaysian glove makers can fully pass through higher costs without hurting volumes, she adds. Maybank keeps a neutral rating on the sector and rates Hartalega and Kossan Rubber Industries at hold. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
